$comment: ADR 0049 §1/§4/§5. Every fixed download is pinned by SHA-256; a mirror that serves other bytes is a failed source. Versions marked 'official latest' were resolved on 2026-11-28 and are recorded here, not followed at run time.

chromium.$comment: Must equal PUPPETEER_REVISIONS.chrome of the bound CLI (cgsVersion), so omp's browser tool finds it instead of downloading.

llvm.$comment: llvm-mingw (ucrt, x86_64): clang, lld and clangd in one archive, the gcc-named wrappers rust's gnu target links with. Only GitHub hosts it; the two proxies are tried only because the SHA-256 makes an untrusted proxy harmless.

rust.$comment: rustup verifies each component against the channel manifest it downloads from the same server, so the manifest itself is pinned here: a server whose channel file hashes differently is skipped.
rust.$comment2: rustup-init.exe exists only for the gnu host, so it bootstraps with --default-toolchain none and then installs the gnullvm toolchain: the gnu host links against libgcc/libgcc_eh, which llvm-mingw does not ship (checked on a Windows guest, 2026-11-28); gnullvm links with llvm-mingw's compiler-rt and libunwind.

languageServers.$comment: pyright and typescript-language-server, with the typescript they need, installed by the bundled bun from desktop/toolchain/lsp-package.json and lsp-bun.lock (integrity hashes; the lock has no registry URL, so any npm mirror serves it).

pip.$comment: Installed after everything else, never blocks start (ADR 0049 §3). requirements.txt carries hashes, so the index need not be trusted.

cgs.$comment: bun add -g @cicori/cgs@<cgsVersion> through the npm mirror that actually has that version.
